text:
Lina (Docs): Heads-up — I'm opening a small PR to clarify the Optimize toolkit examples for short-seq workloads. Will add a concise example showing micro-batching + kv prefetch with a 4-bit quant profile. PR shortly: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234

Michael (Eng): SG. Can you include a before/after perf note and call out any SDK param renames?

Sam (ML): If you show q4 usage, add a brief compatibility note about older GPUs and offload. I can paste a tiny quant_profile snippet.

Lina (Docs): Draft snippet (first pass):
```python
from redwood import OptimizeClient
client = OptimizeClient()
resp = client.generate(model='rwkv-7b', prompt='Translate:', max_tokens=64, batch_size=8, prefetch_kv=True, quant_profile='q4_0')
print(resp.text)
```
Is that OK or do we need to match current SDK names?

Michael (Eng): tiny nit: SDK param is kv_prefetch not prefetch_kv. Also for streaming clients use micro_batch instead of batch_size.

Lina (Docs): Good catch — updated snippet:
```python
from redwood.optimize import OptimizeClient
client = OptimizeClient()
resp = client.generate(model='rwkv-7b', prompt='Translate:', max_tokens=64, micro_batch=8, kv_prefetch=True, quant_profile='q4_0')
print(resp.text)
```

Emma (Product): Can we add one sentence on tradeoffs? e.g. micro_batch increases throughput but can add tail latency for single-user interactive flows.

Sam (ML): Putting the quant_profile YAML I'll suggest for docs/examples:
```yaml
name: q4_0
bits: 4
per_channel: true
compatible_ops: ['matmul', 'linear']
notes: 'Prefer on T4/A100; fallback to fp16 on unsupported hardware'
```

Lina (Docs): Adding that under the example and a short callout about hardware fallbacks. Also adding a migration note: "prefetch_kv -> kv_prefetch" and "batch_size -> micro_batch" for anyone upgrading older examples.

Lina (Docs): CI note — when we change examples we need the snippet-tests and link-checker to pass. @ci-bot can you run the example lint on PR #1234? :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: Example lint started for PR #1234 — running snippet-tests, link-check, md-lint.

ci-bot: snippet-tests failed: examples/optkit/shortseq.py line 3 — import changed to redwood.optimize. See error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'

Michael (Eng): That usually happens in the test harness. Use `from redwood.optimize import OptimizeClient` to match the test env. Also make sure example requirements include optimize-client in the test matrix.

Lina (Docs): Updated import and pushed a tiny migration blurb: "If you used prefetch_kv in v0.x, switch to kv_prefetch; micro_batch replaces batch_size for streaming." Pushed to PR.

Sam (ML): One more suggestion — add a compact table under the example showing recommended micro_batch + kv_prefetch toggles for common latency SLOs: interactive (<200ms), conversational (200-500ms), batch (>500ms). Keeps guidance actionable.

Lina (Docs): Good idea — I'll add a 3-row table and keep it short. Pushing final tweaks now.

ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #1234. Merging. :tada:

Emma (Product): Thanks y'all! Can someone paste the final docs URL so I can include it in the release notes?

Lina (Docs): Final page published: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/shortseq-microbatch — added to changelog and release draft.

Michael (Eng): FYI we'll enable a telemetry flag next week to track quick adoption of the new params.

Sam (ML): I'll follow up with a short internal note about quant_profile constraints and a pointer to the model-compatibility matrix.

Lina (Docs): Closing thread — thanks for the quick turnaround everyone. :pray:
